title: A NumericRange iterator computes knownSize in the element type, giving negative or too-small sizes for Byte, Short, Int and Long ranges wider than half the type
oracle: knownSize is -1 or the number of remaining elements; BigInt model of the range
generator: wave4/harness/collections3/RangeDiff.scala: NumericRange over Byte, Short, Int and Long with bounds at the type extremes; iterator knownSize compared with the model's count
signature: NR[Byte] | | it.knownSize | val -> val (also NR[Short], NR[Int], NR[Long])
seed: seed 2, 100 s run; case number not recorded
detail: NumericRangeIterator.knownSize (src/library/scala/collection/immutable/NumericRange.scala, class NumericRangeIterator) is num.toInt((lastElement - _next) / step) + 1, with the subtraction done by the Integral of the element type. For NumericRange.inclusive[Byte](-128, 57, 5), 38 elements, 57 - (-128) wraps to -71 and knownSize is -13, a value the knownSize contract does not allow. For Short, Int and Long ranges wider than half the type it is 0 or 1 for a longer iterator: NumericRange.inclusive(Long.MinValue, Long.MaxValue, Long.MaxValue) has 3 elements and reports 1. Consumers that size themselves from knownSize then truncate (toVector) or, with 0, return nothing (toList, mkString). A Byte range over more than 127 values is ordinary; the wider types need extreme bounds.
fix_sketch: Use the range's own length (already computed without overflow) minus the number of elements consumed, or return -1 when the difference cannot be represented. No compatibility cost.
prior: none found for the iterator; LI2 and LI3 (retronym/scala#569, #556, #655) are the same arithmetic-in-the-element-type mistake in contains and length
